chief_complaint: fever, back pain, and leg weakness
hpi_details: 65F presents with 3 weeks of worsening mid-back pain, low-grade fevers, and new-onset weakness and numbness in her bilateral lower extremities. She has a history of poorly controlled diabetes.

investigation_events.title: STAT contrast-enhanced spine MRI
investigation_events.availability_message: The STAT spine MRI is now available; blood cultures, empiric antibiotics, and neurosurgical consultation should not be delayed.

results.test: Contrast-enhanced thoracic and lumbar spine MRI
results.value: Posterior epidural rim-enhancing collection from T7 through T10 causing severe thecal-sac compression and cord edema

core_concepts: Triad of fever, spinal pain, and neurologic deficits.
common_misconceptions: Treating only as musculoskeletal back pain because fever might be mild.
dangerous_errors: Discharging patients with new neuro deficits without an urgent MRI.
management_principles: STAT full-spine MRI with contrast, blood cultures, empiric antibiotics, emergent neurosurgical consult.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) Clinical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 65F with worsening back pain, fever, and new leg weakness.
reference_soap.objective: Point tenderness over thoracic spine. 4/5 strength in bilateral lower extremities. Decreased sensation below umbilicus.
reference_soap.plan: STAT MRI thoracic/lumbar spine with contrast. Neurosurgery consult. Blood cultures, then IV Vancomycin and Ceftriaxone.

learning_objectives: Identify the triad of spinal epidural abscess and order urgent MRI.

teaching.one_liner: Fever, localized back pain, and progressive neurologic deficits (leg weakness) necessitating urgent MRI.

must_ask.say: Where exactly is the back pain, and is it constant or does it come and go?
Have you had any fevers over the past few weeks?
Have you noticed any weakness or numbness in your legs?
Have you had any trouble controlling your bladder or bowels?
Do you have diabetes, or any recent infections, injections, or IV drug use?

history.answer: My mid-back has been hurting terribly for three weeks, and over the past two days both of my legs have become weak and numb.
The pain is right in the middle of my back between my shoulder blades, and it does not shoot down past my knees.
It started gradually about three weeks ago without any heavy lifting, fall, or injury.
It is a deep, severe, constant ache that reaches an eight out of ten in intensity.
Any movement, coughing, or bending makes it much worse, and lying down does not relieve it.
Yes, the pain stays severe even when I lie flat, and it wakes me up repeatedly at night.
history.topic: Pain at rest and night pain

history.answer: I feel stiff when trying to move because of the pain, but it does not ease after thirty minutes or with activity.
About two days ago, my legs became clumsy and weak, and my legs and feet started feeling numb.
The skin around my groin and private area still feels normal, and I haven't had any accidents with my urine or stool.
Walking makes my legs feel heavy and unsteady, and bending forward or sitting down does not relieve the pain.
I have felt feverish on and off with low fevers over the last two weeks, but no drenching night sweats or major weight loss.
No, I have never had cancer or any tumors.
I haven't had any spinal injections, acupuncture, or recent operations, and I don't use IV drugs, but my diabetes has been poorly controlled.
I have not been diagnosed with osteoporosis, I don't take steroid medications, and I haven't had any recent falls.
No, I don't have belly pain, throbbing in my abdomen, or any burning or blood when I pass urine.
I have not had red painful eyes, heel pain, chronic diarrhea, or skin rashes like psoriasis.
I took over-the-counter acetaminophen and ibuprofen, but neither of them helped the pain at all.
Since retiring I spend most of my time resting at home, but this constant pain and leg weakness have been terribly frightening.
At first I assumed I had just strained a muscle in my back, but it keeps getting worse.
I am terrified that I might lose the use of my legs completely and end up paralyzed.
I really hope I can get an MRI today to find out exactly what is wrong with my spine.
I have had type 2 diabetes for about ten years, and my sugar levels have been higher than usual lately.
I have never had any surgeries or needed to stay in the hospital before.
I take metformin 1000 milligrams twice a day for my diabetes.
I have no known allergies to any medicines.
I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only have a small sip of wine on very rare special occasions.
I am retired and live at home with my husband.
My mother had diabetes and my father had high blood pressure, but no one in my family had spinal infections or paralysis.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, heart rate 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 38.0 degrees Celsius, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Alert 65-year-old female lying supine in bed, appearing uncomfortable and guarding her back with movement.
Severe focal point tenderness and percussion tenderness over the mid-thoracic spinous processes; straight leg raise is negative bilaterally.
Thoracic and lumbar range of motion is severely restricted in flexion and extension due to sharp back pain.
Symmetric 4/5 motor strength throughout bilateral lower extremities; upper extremity strength is intact at 5/5.
Decreased light touch and pinprick sensation bilaterally below the level of the umbilicus.
Brisk 3+ bilateral patellar and Achilles deep tendon reflexes, with bilateral positive Babinski signs.
Normal anal sphincter resting tone and voluntary contraction; perianal sensation is intact.
Abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended, with no palpable pulsatile abdominal mass.
No costovertebral angle tenderness on gentle percussion bilaterally.
